title: AgentVQA finds visual-state tracking limits in multimodal agents
dek: An offline benchmark spans five interactive domains and isolates grounding failures that task-success scores can obscure.
evidence: Original benchmark paper; offline multiple-choice proxy for online execution
takeaway: Evaluate temporal state and object grounding before attributing multimodal agent failures to planning.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: A model can describe one screenshot accurately yet miss what changed after a click or how two objects relate in space.

paragraphs: Visual action needs state tracking: A model can describe one screenshot accurately yet miss what changed after a click or how two objects relate in space.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Researchers curated 1,000 difficult visual questions from 23 datasets covering web agents, robotics, egocentric video, games and spatial planning.
The test turns interactive-world observations into repeatable offline questions, permitting broad VLM comparisons without rerunning every environment.

paragraphs: AgentVQA benchmark: Researchers curated 1,000 difficult visual questions from 23 datasets covering web agents, robotics, egocentric video, games and spatial planning.
Offline proxy: The test turns interactive-world observations into repeatable offline questions, permitting broad VLM comparisons without rerunning every environment.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: The best evaluated model reached 58.5% accuracy; reported failures centered on localization, motion, state changes and 3D relationships.
The authors report that offline rankings track related online results, but an offline question cannot reveal action recovery, permission handling or long-horizon tool use.

paragraphs: 22-model evaluation: The best evaluated model reached 58.5% accuracy; reported failures centered on localization, motion, state changes and 3D relationships.
Proxy limitation: The authors report that offline rankings track related online results, but an offline question cannot reveal action recovery, permission handling or long-horizon tool use.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: A seemingly poor plan may actually reflect an incorrect perception of the current interface or environment state.
Test what moved, which button currently exists, what changed after an action and whether the visual state supports the next proposed tool call.

paragraphs: Don't overdiagnose planning: A seemingly poor plan may actually reflect an incorrect perception of the current interface or environment state.
Add temporal evals: Test what moved, which button currently exists, what changed after an action and whether the visual state supports the next proposed tool call.
